intervention_name: Individual placement and support (IPS) plus treatment as usual
intervention_description: Six months of IPS delivered by a vocational specialist embedded in the EPPIC clinical team, in addition to standard EPPIC treatment

Treatment as usual: referral to external government-contracted employment agencies, plus standard EPPIC treatment (medical management, out-patient case management, group programme, peer and family support)

Both randomised arms merged: the 18-month sample analysed by clarke2023 contains 54 participants from the vocational (IPS) arm and 46 from TAU (clarke2023 Table 4, p. 775), with treatment group entered only as a covariate. Half the merged cohort therefore received six months of IPS.

Whole recruited cohort: consecutive acute admissions to two Chicago hospitals, followed naturalistically at approximately 2, 4.5, 7.5, 10, 15 and 20 years. No allocation. No whole-cohort employment count is reported in either F04 report, so this row carries no result.
Patients with schizophrenia prescribed antipsychotic medication at the 20-year follow-up assessment, irrespective of earlier medication status. Naturalistic, not allocated.
Patients with schizophrenia not prescribed antipsychotic medication at the 20-year follow-up assessment, irrespective of earlier medication status. Naturalistic, not allocated.
Whole recruited cohort of 150 out-patients with severe mental illness attending one public hospital; observational, no allocation and no vocational intervention
